doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

title: Where melodies start
summary: Davis describes melody-, harmony- and rhythm-first composing approaches.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well said. I want to talk about compositional inspiration for a moment. I was looking at your catalogue and I’m assuming these are your tunes or maybe your son’s. There was this song called “A Life Lived” from 9/11 time, and then on the other spectrum there’s something called “Stomper” which you described as a Steely Dan meets Jaco meets Dave Matthews.
That’s very generous of me to describe that that way.
So what inspires a melodic line for you? Where does it start?

I’m not sure where it starts. I mean I think there’s a couple different approaches that I use and one is melody based, you know where the first thing that you come up with is a melody that anybody could — you just have something in your head and it could be a fragment of something else you’d heard that day, it could be — it could come from anywhere. It could be oh I had MLB network on and they had this like goofball theme and like for some reason it stuck in my head and then two weeks later you have something that resembles that or you know, whatever it might be, it just kind of comes out organically.
